meta.title: Multi-site B2B quote-to-order in one flow
assumptions: Delta metrics are placeholders until the customer confirms baseline figures in discovery.
UI labels and locators are illustrative for a Communications Cloud demo org. They are marked verified: false; confirm them with the headless smoke test against your org.
Permission set Demo_B2B_Sales is a demo-specific example; replace it with the permission sets your org uses.

situation.criticalBusinessIssue: Hit this year's B2B connectivity revenue target while multi-site deals keep slipping into the next quarter.
problems: Multi-site quotes are assembled in spreadsheets and re-keyed into the order system.
Discount approvals run over email, without an audit trail.
Order errors surface only at provisioning, which delays activation and billing.
specificCapabilities: Configure a multi-site offer from the product catalog, with catalog rules enforced
Price the quote in the opportunity, with discount approval in the same flow
Convert the accepted quote into an order without re-keying
Show order decomposition, so fulfilment sees exactly what was sold

delta.statement: A shorter quote-to-order cycle and fewer reworked orders in the B2B segment.

storyline.opening: Your team told us that multi-site deals take too long to quote and that orders come back for rework. In the next 30 minutes we follow one deal for {{vars.accountName}} from configuration to a submitted order, in one system.

lastThingFirst.description: We start with the result: the {{vars.accountName}} deal for {{vars.siteCount}} sites, already converted to an order, with every order line traceable to the catalog offer it came from.

keyTakeaways: One flow from catalog to order: no spreadsheets and no re-keying.
Catalog rules stop invalid configurations before the quote, not at provisioning.
Fulfilment sees exactly what sales sold, line by line.

closing.summary: We followed one multi-site deal from configuration to a submitted order, with the catalog enforcing the rules and every order line traceable.
nextSteps: Agree baseline figures for quote-to-order lead time and order rework.
Workshop on catalog rules for your top three multi-site offers.
Technical deep dive on order decomposition and the fulfilment integration.

personas.name: Ewa Nowak
personas.goal: Send a correct multi-site quote on the same day.

personas.name: Piotr Zieliński
personas.goal: Receive orders that do not need rework.

scenes.title: The result first: a submitted multi-site order
scenes.objective: Show the end result before any configuration.
scenes.tell: Before we build anything, here is where we will end: the {{vars.accountName}} deal, already an order.
scenes.wowMoment: Every order line links back to the quote line and the catalog offer it came from.
scenes.valueStatement: Sales and fulfilment look at the same deal, so nothing is re-keyed or lost between them.
discoveryQuestions: Where does a multi-site deal wait longest today: quoting, approval or order entry?

steps.title: Open recent opportunities
steps.talkTrack: We open the recent opportunities list.
steps.fallback: Open the opportunity from global search.

steps.title: Show the deal and its order
steps.talkTrack: This is the {{vars.accountName}} opportunity. It already has an accepted quote and a submitted order. Each order line came from the quote, and each quote line came from the catalog.
steps.fallback: Show the screenshot of the submitted order from the last headless run.

scenes.title: Configure and price a multi-site quote
scenes.objective: Prove that a multi-site offer is configured from the catalog, with its rules enforced.
scenes.tell: Ewa now builds the same quote from scratch, the way she would on a normal Tuesday.
scenes.wowMoment: The catalog blocks an invalid combination before the quote is priced.
scenes.valueStatement: Quotes are right the first time, so approvals and orders do not bounce back.
discoveryQuestions: Which offer rules does your team check by hand today?
Who approves discounts above list price, and how?

objections.objection: Our catalog is too complex to model.
objections.response: We model the top multi-site offers first and add the rest in waves; the catalog workshop in the next steps sets the scope.

steps.title: Open the quote
steps.talkTrack: From the opportunity, Ewa opens the quote she started this morning.
steps.fallback: Open the quote from the Recent Items list.

steps.title: Start configuration
steps.talkTrack: She opens the configurator. Everything you see here comes from the product catalog, not from a spreadsheet.
steps.fallback: Show the configured quote from the first scene and talk through the rules.

steps.title: Set the number of sites
steps.talkTrack: {{vars.accountName}} has {{vars.siteCount}} sites. Ewa sets that once, and the configuration applies to every site.
steps.fallback: Explain the multi-site pricing on the order from the first scene.

steps.title: Show a catalog rule
steps.talkTrack: Watch what happens when she picks an add-on that is not allowed with this access type. The catalog stops it here, not at provisioning.
steps.notes: Pick the add-on that your catalog marks as incompatible, then add the click and its locator here.
steps.fallback: Show the rule in the catalog's rule list instead.

scenes.title: Convert the accepted quote to an order
scenes.objective: Show the hand-off from sales to fulfilment without re-keying.
scenes.tell: The customer accepts the quote. Piotr, the order manager, takes it from here.
scenes.wowMoment: The order is decomposed into fulfilment lines automatically.
scenes.valueStatement: Fulfilment receives exactly what was sold, so activation and billing start without rework.
discoveryQuestions: How many orders come back for correction each month?

steps.title: Create the order
steps.talkTrack: One click turns the accepted quote into an order.
steps.fallback: Open the order created for the first scene.

steps.title: Show order decomposition
steps.talkTrack: This is what fulfilment sees: each commercial line broken down into the technical lines that downstream systems need.
steps.fallback: Show the decomposition screenshot from the last headless run.

manualSteps: Load the multi-site B2B offers into the product catalog (EPC). Use the omnistudio-epc-catalog-generate skill to author the catalog DataPacks.
Create the accepted quote and the submitted order for the first scene, for example during a rehearsal run.
Create permission set Demo_B2B_Sales with access to quotes and orders, or replace it in personas[].org.permissionSets.
